blocks.text: 10. Measurements
10.1 Samples
The BactoSense can measure manually collected grab samples using the manual sampling device, and also sample automatically from a connected water source using the online sampling device.
blocks.html: The BactoSense can measure manually collected grab samples using the manual sampling device, and also sample automatically from a connected water source using the online sampling device.

blocks.text: Sample types and pretreatments:
blocks.html: Sample types and pretreatments:

blocks.text: Raw waters and especially surface waters must be filtered with a 20 µm filter. Particles can block the internal filters and damage the instrument. Clear water expected to be potable usually does not need filtering. Sparkling water and soft drinks cannot be measured by the instrument. Water with a high concentration of chlorine can affect the results of the measurement. The sample and operating conditions listed in Technical data must be fulfilled.
blocks.html:
• Raw waters and especially surface waters must be filtered with a 20 µm filter. Particles can block the internal filters and damage the instrument. Clear water expected to be potable usually does not need filtering.
  • Sparkling water and soft drinks cannot be measured by the instrument.
  • Water with a high concentration of chlorine can affect the results of the measurement.
  • The sample and operating conditions listed in Technical data must be fulfilled.

blocks.text: 10.2 Measuring automatically in Online mode

Measuring in Online mode describes a configuration, in which the BactoSense is connected to a water source using the online sampling device, and automatically draws and measures a sample at predefined intervals.
blocks.html: Measuring in Online mode describes a configuration, in which the BactoSense is connected to a water source using the online sampling device, and automatically draws and measures a sample at predefined intervals.

blocks.text: If you want to measure manually collected grab samples instead, refer to Measuring in manual mode .
blocks.html: If you want to measure manually collected grab samples instead, refer to Measuring in manual mode.

blocks.text: For different intervals or selected weekdays, see Advanced scheduling .
blocks.html: For different intervals or selected weekdays, see Advanced scheduling.

blocks.text: 10.2.1 Configuring and starting automatic online measurements
The following instructions show how to configure and start automatic online measurements using the online sampling device.
blocks.html: The following instructions show how to configure and start automatic online measurements using the online sampling device.

blocks.text: WORK STEP ADDITIONAL INFO / IMAGES 1. Make sure the online sampling device is tightly installed as described in Installation of the online sampling device . If you have the manual sampling device installed and want to change to the online sampling device, refer to Removal of the manual sampling device to remove the manual sampling device and Installation of the online sampling device to install the online sampling device. 2. Navigate to the Home screen of the BactoSense user interface. 3. On the Home screen, press Mode . On the Mode selection screen, tap Online mode , then press Back to return to the Home screen. The current mode is highlighted. Tapping a mode switches to it immediately. If a measurement is running, press Stop it to abort it, or press Wait and select the mode again after it has finished. If Instrument validation can't be used with Online mode. Do you want to disable Instrument validation? appears, press Yes . If the Home screen then asks Do you want to start Online mode? , press No and continue with the next step; Yes restarts the series with the previously saved Online mode settings. 4. Press Start on the Home screen to open the online measurement wizard. 5. Under Protocol, make sure the checkbox for “Online Sampling Device (with Backflush)” is checked. 6. Enter a sample name by tapping into the Sample name text field. 7. Select the desired gate to be applied to the measurements by tapping into the Gates text field. Generally, default TCC and ICC gates are used. Use user-defined gates if your application requires it. Creating and adjusting gates is described in Results and Data Analysis . 8. Press the Next button. 9. If the weekly schedule editor is displayed, press Back to return to the simple interval schedule. Select the measurement interval using the wheel on the right hand side. The measurement interval describes the time between different measurements and can be as short as 30 min and as long as 6 hours. 10. If needed, delay the starting time by unchecking Start immediately and choosing a specific start time. The time setting of the BactoSense is described in Date and time . 11. Press the Start button. During the measurement, the current estimate of the cell concentration is displayed in the action bar under “Last”. 12. After each measurement, the time series graph is updated. For more details press the View results button. 13. If you want to stop an online measurement series, refer to Terminating automatic online measurements .

blocks.text: 10.2.2 Terminating automatic online measurements
Follow the steps below to terminate a measurement series in Online mode.
blocks.html: Follow the steps below to terminate a measurement series in Online mode.

blocks.text: WORK STEP ADDITIONAL INFO / IMAGES 1. In Online mode, tap the plot on the Home screen to open the online chart. Press Stop. 2. Confirm the message to stop the Online mode measurement series. 3. If a measurement is running, you can select whether you want to abort it immediately, or wait for completion. 4. blocks.text: 10.2.4 Advanced scheduling

Use advanced scheduling when measurements must run at different intervals or on selected weekdays. A weekly schedule combines one or more rules, each with its own protocol, measurement name, gates and timing. The same weekly plan repeats until you change or stop it.
blocks.html: Use advanced scheduling when measurements must run at different intervals or on selected weekdays. A weekly schedule combines one or more rules, each with its own protocol, measurement name, gates and timing. The same weekly plan repeats until you change or stop it.

blocks.text: Advanced scheduling requires an activated Management Package or Scientific Package. If Advanced is unavailable, check the package status under Settings → System settings → Upgrades ; see Upgrade Packages . Before starting, install the online sampling device and check the instrument's date and time .
blocks.html: Advanced scheduling requires an activated Management Package or Scientific Package. If Advanced is unavailable, check the package status under Settings → System settings → Upgrades; see Upgrade Packages. Before starting, install the online sampling device and check the instrument's date and time.

blocks.text: Create a weekly schedule

WORK STEP ADDITIONAL INFO / IMAGES 1. Follow steps 1–8 of Configuring and starting automatic online measurements to choose Online mode, the protocol, sample name and gates. Press Next to reach the scheduling screen. 2. Press Advanced . If a weekly schedule is already configured, the rule editor may open directly. Figure 10-3 shows the Advanced control on the simple interval screen. 3. Select a rule in the left-hand list to edit it, or press New rule to add one. Select an unwanted rule and press Delete to remove it from the draft. Review the existing rules before adding another; all rules contribute to the weekly schedule. 4. Set Name , Protocol and Gate for the selected rule. Name labels the resulting measurements. Choose gates compatible with the installed cartridge. Maintenance protocols that do not need gates hide this field. 5. Choose 30 minutes , 1 hour , 2 hours , Daily or Custom . The interval presets repeat every day. Daily schedules one run per day at the chosen Start time . Use Custom to select weekdays, another interval or a time window. 6. For Custom , set Start time , select the required Days and set Interval in minutes. Press Set time range to choose the daily window, then confirm with OK . Scroll the fields below the frequency buttons to see Interval , Set time range and Range . Figures 10-4 and 10-5 show the same rule before and after scrolling. 7. Repeat steps 3–6 for any additional rules. Press Preview . Select a gate if Preview is unavailable because one is missing. If preview reports a conflict, return to the rules and adjust their times or intervals so protocols have time to finish. 8. Select each weekday in the preview and check the generated entries. Select an entry to inspect its Time , Name , Protocol and Gate . The preview can include automatically inserted cleaning protocols during long gaps. Review these alongside measurement entries; see Figure 10-6. 9. Make any individual changes described below, then press Save to apply the weekly schedule. Changes to rules and preview entries remain a draft until you press Save . 10. At Start scheduler now? , press Yes to start the saved plan, or No to save it without starting a stopped scheduler. Check the Home screen to confirm the operating state. To stop an active series, follow Terminating automatic online measurements .

blocks.text: 10.3 Measuring in manual mode

Measuring in manual mode describes a configuration, in which the manual sampling device is connected to the BactoSense, and the operator attaches individual grab samples collected in 5 mL screw cap tubes to the instrument.
blocks.html: Measuring in manual mode describes a configuration, in which the manual sampling device is connected to the BactoSense, and the operator attaches individual grab samples collected in 5 mL screw cap tubes to the instrument.

blocks.text: 10.3.1 Performing a measurement in manual mode
The following instructions show how to configure and start a measurement in manual mode.
blocks.html: The following instructions show how to configure and start a measurement in manual mode.

blocks.text: WORK STEP ADDITIONAL INFO / IMAGES 1. Make sure the manual sampling device is tightly installed as described in Installation of the manual sampling device . 2. If the manual sampling device has been newly installed or the instrument has been switched off or idle for more than 3 days, it is recommended to clean the sampling device. If a Washstation is available, follow the procedure in Clean manual sampling device with Washstation , otherwise the procedure in Clean manual sampling device with basic cleaning . 3. If a cleaning of the manual sampling device has been conducted (see previous step), it is recommended to perform a prime prior to measuring the sample. Follow the procedure in Performing a Prime . 4. Navigate to the Home screen of the BactoSense user interface. 5. On the Home screen, press Mode . On the Mode selection screen, tap Manual mode . Press Back , then Measure to open the measurement wizard. The current mode is highlighted. Tapping a mode switches to it immediately. If an Online mode series is active, confirm Do you really want to stop Online mode? with Yes . If a measurement is running, press Stop it to abort it, or press Wait and select the mode again after it has finished. Manual mode cannot be selected while PLC mode is active (see Digital inputs configuration and PLC mode ). 6. Select Water Analysis from the list of available protocols. If you want technical replicates, select the number of replicates in Replications column. By default, one sample is measured. If more replicates are configured, multiple samples are drawn from the same sample tube. 7. Enter a sample name by tapping into the Sample name text field, entering the name and pressing OK. 8. Check whether your desired gate is configured in the Gates field. If you wish to use another gate, tap into the Gates field and select the desired gate from the available options (depending on the cartridge installed). Generally, default TCC and ICC gates are used. Use user-defined gates if your application requires it. Creating and adjusting gates is described in Results and Data Analysis . 9. Press the Next button. 10. Attach a 5 mL screw-cap tube containing 2 – 5 mL of sample to the manual sampling device. 11. Press the Start button. The estimated protocol duration and expected termination timepoint are displayed. The current state of the measurement is indicated in the top bar (e.g. Initializing, Mixing...) 12. After finishing the measurement, press Next to view the results. Results are explained in Measurement results . 13. If you want to proceed with the next measurement, press the New button. 14. If you want to see previous measurement results, press the View results button. 15. If you want to rename, regate or export the measurement, refer to the instructions in following sections. 16. If you don’t want to measure more samples and the instrument will be idle or switched off, perform a cleaning of the manual sampling device. If a Washstation is available, follow the procedure in Clean manual sampling device with Washstation , otherwise the procedure in Clean manual sampling device with basic cleaning .

blocks.text: 10.4 Renaming measurements
Measurements can be renamed from their result details view.
blocks.html: Measurements can be renamed from their result details view.

blocks.text: WORK STEP 1. On the Home screen, press Settings, then Logs, and select Results (manual mode) or Results (online mode). 2. In the results list, select the measurement you want to rename. Exception: If you want to rename a group of replicates (see Working with measurement replicates ), long- press on the group of replicates and then press the rename button. 3. In the result details view, press the Rename button (see Measurement results ). 4. A keyboard and text field with the current sample name will appear. Use the keyboard to change the sample name and press OK.

blocks.text: 10.5 Working with measurement replicates
When working in manual mode, analysis protocols can be repeated. This is particularly useful for generating technical replicates of a single sample.
blocks.html: When working in manual mode, analysis protocols can be repeated. This is particularly useful for generating technical replicates of a single sample.

blocks.text: The number of replicates can be selected when configuring a manual measurement, as described in Performing a measurement in manual mode . In the manual mode results list, replicates are grouped into one entry, and the number in brackets next to the sample name indicates the number of replicates. In this view, the results shown for the replicate group consist of average and standard deviation. Individual replicate measurements can be accessed by pressing on the replicate group. Replicate groups can easily be renamed, deleted, exported or regated after a long-press on the replicate group in the manual mode results list.

blocks.text: 10.7 Filtering measurements

Filters limit the results list to the measurements you need. You can filter by date range, by measurement name and, when BactoSwitch is enabled, by BactoSwitch line. When you combine filters, only measurements that match all of them are listed. The filters search all measurements stored on the instrument.
blocks.html: Filters limit the results list to the measurements you need. You can filter by date range, by measurement name and, when BactoSwitch is enabled, by BactoSwitch line. When you combine filters, only measurements that match all of them are listed. The filters search all measurements stored on the instrument.

blocks.text: WORK STEP ADDITIONAL INFO / IMAGES 1. On the Home screen, press Results . The list shows the results of the current operating mode: Online mode results or Manual mode results . To open the list for the other mode, press Settings , then Logs , and select Results (online mode) or Results (manual mode) . 2. Press Filter . The Filter results screen opens. The fields on the left show the current filters. 3. To filter by date, tap the field under Start date and select the first day in the calendar. Tap the time field below it and set the hour and minute with the wheels. Set End date and its time in the same way. Both limits are included: measurements up to the end of the selected end minute are listed. The end cannot be earlier than the start. Without a date filter, the range runs from the oldest to the newest measurement. 4. To filter by name, tap the field under Filter by name , enter part of the measurement name and press OK . The list keeps every measurement whose name contains this text, regardless of upper or lower case. For example, tap finds “Tap Water Zürich”. None means that no name filter is set. To remove the name filter, delete the text and press OK . 5. To filter by BactoSwitch line, press Filter by stream , select the line and press Confirm . This button is only shown when BactoSwitch is enabled. Each line is listed with its name and stream number; the button then shows Filtered by stream #n . Only Online mode measurements sampled through BactoSwitch belong to a line, so all other measurements are hidden while this filter is active. To remove the line filter, select the highlighted line again and press Confirm . 6. Press OK to apply the filters and return to the results list. The action bar shows the date range and any active line and name filters. If no measurement matches, No measurements to display appears; press Change filters to adjust the filters.

WORK STEPADDITIONAL INFO / IMAGES
1.On the Home screen, press Results.The list shows the results of the current operating mode: Online mode results or Manual mode results. To open the list for the other mode, press Settings, then Logs, and select Results (online mode) or Results (manual mode).
2.Press Filter.The Filter results screen opens. The fields on the left show the current filters.
3.To filter by date, tap the field under Start date and select the first day in the calendar. Tap the time field below it and set the hour and minute with the wheels. Set End date and its time in the same way.Both limits are included: measurements up to the end of the selected end minute are listed. The end cannot be earlier than the start. Without a date filter, the range runs from the oldest to the newest measurement.
4.To filter by name, tap the field under Filter by name, enter part of the measurement name and press OK.The list keeps every measurement whose name contains this text, regardless of upper or lower case. For example, tap finds “Tap Water Zürich”. None means that no name filter is set. To remove the name filter, delete the text and press OK.
5.To filter by BactoSwitch line, press Filter by stream, select the line and press Confirm.This button is only shown when BactoSwitch is enabled. Each line is listed with its name and stream number; the button then shows Filtered by stream #n. Only Online mode measurements sampled through BactoSwitch belong to a line, so all other measurements are hidden while this filter is active. To remove the line filter, select the highlighted line again and press Confirm.
6.Press OK to apply the filters and return to the results list.The action bar shows the date range and any active line and name filters. If no measurement matches, No measurements to display appears; press Change filters to adjust the filters.

blocks.text: Clear the filters Press Reset on the Filter results screen to remove the name and line filters and restore the full date range. Filters in the Manual mode results are cleared when you return to the Home screen. In Online mode, the name and line filters remain active, including on the online chart (see Reviewing automatic online measurements ), until you reset them.

CLEAR THE FILTERS

Press Reset on the Filter results screen to remove the name and line filters and restore the full date range. Filters in the Manual mode results are cleared when you return to the Home screen. In Online mode, the name and line filters remain active, including on the online chart (see Reviewing automatic online measurements), until you reset them.

blocks.text: 10.8 Exporting measurements

There are multiple ways to retrieve measurement data. Retrieval via HTTP, HTTPS, FTP and the web interface are described in Data Access and Export and Web User Interface . In this section, data export to a USB drive is described.
blocks.html: There are multiple ways to retrieve measurement data. Retrieval via HTTP, HTTPS, FTP and the web interface are described in Data Access and Export and Web User Interface. In this section, data export to a USB drive is described.

blocks.text: 10.8.1 Export to a USB drive
It is possible to export selected or all measurements to a USB flash drive.
blocks.html: It is possible to export selected or all measurements to a USB flash drive.

blocks.text: Make sure your USB flash drive is formatted in FAT32 format.
blocks.html: Make sure your USB flash drive is formatted in FAT32 format.

blocks.text: WORK STEP 1. On the Home screen, press Settings, then Logs, and select Results (manual mode) or Results (online mode). 2. In the results list: • Press Export series, choose the date range and optional name filter, then press OK to export a series. • Long-press a replicate group, then press Export to export that group. • Open a single measurement, then press Export to export only that measurement. 3. In the folder name field, the name of the target folder which will be created on the USB drive is shown. Change the name if desired. 4. Insert a USB stick with enough available memory. Press Refresh list to display the connected USB stick. 5. Export options • press Export results to export only the basic results (see details in the user interface) • press Export all to export results, raw data and diagnostic information (see details in the user interface) 6. Wait for the export to complete and then press OK.
blocks.html:
WORK STEP
1.On the Home screen, press Settings, then Logs, and select Results (manual mode) or Results (online mode).
2.In the results list:
• Press Export series, choose the date range and optional name filter, then press OK to export a series.
• Long-press a replicate group, then press Export to export that group.
• Open a single measurement, then press Export to export only that measurement.
3.In the folder name field, the name of the target folder which will be created on the USB drive is shown. Change the name if desired.
4.Insert a USB stick with enough available memory. Press Refresh list to display the connected USB stick.
5.Export options
• press Export results to export only the basic results (see details in the user interface)
• press Export all to export results, raw data and diagnostic information (see details in the user interface)
6.Wait for the export to complete and then press OK.

blocks.text: 10.9 Available analysis and maintenance protocols
10.9.1 Overview of protocols in manual mode
Operators can choose between two analysis protocols in manual mode.
blocks.html: Operators can choose between two analysis protocols in manual mode.

blocks.html: Table 10-1 Analysis protocols for manual mode

blocks.text: PROTOCOL NAME PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION Water Analysis Analyze a water sample and finish with a cleaning cycle. If several replications are executed, the cleaning step is executed only once, at the end. A prime is executed automatically between replicates. Beads Analysis This protocol is intended for the analysis of calibration beads and is used with the Validation Kit. The protocol automatically finishes with a cleaning cycle. If several replications are executed, the cleaning step is executed only once, at the end.

blocks.text: Maintenance protocols can be executed before or between analysis protocols, to prepare, flush, or clean the system. In manual mode, the following maintenance protocols are available:
blocks.html: Maintenance protocols can be executed before or between analysis protocols, to prepare, flush, or clean the system. In manual mode, the following maintenance protocols are available:

blocks.text: Table 10-2 Maintenance protocols for manual mode
blocks.html: Table 10-2 Maintenance protocols for manual mode

blocks.text: PROTOCOL NAME PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION Clean Optics Launches a cleaning step that washes all components in contact with the sample inside the BactoSense, except the sampling device. Clean Sampling Device with Washstation Cleans the manual sampling device such that the outside filter, the needle's interior and exterior can be fully washed between measurements, after a dirty sample or in case of filter blockage. The Washstation device must be mounted on the manual sampling device and a cartridge must be installed for this protocol to appear. This protocol has a higher disinfection power than the Clean Sampling Device protocol and should therefore be preferred. Using the Washstation is the best way to keep the manual sampling device clean and to avoid cross- contaminations. Instructions for this protocol can be found in Clean manual sampling device with Washstation . Clean Sampling Device Cleans the sampling device so that the external filter and the needle’s interior can be washed after an extremely loaded sample or in case of filter blockage. Instructions for this protocol can be found in Clean manual sampling device with basic cleaning . Fill Tubing Fills all tubing carrying reagents from the cartridge, to remove bubbles in the tubing. Cleans optics at the end of the process. Prime and Clean Optics Fills the tubing with liquid from the sample. Helps to dilute any residues after a clean sampling device for instance. Is finished by the cleaning step. Prime Loads sample into the instrument. Instructions can be found in Performing a Prime .

blocks.text: 10.9.3 Performing a Prime
Priming preconditions the BactoSense with the sample. Priming can be used to reduce the carryover of cells or unwanted substances, and takes approximately 5 minutes.
blocks.html: Priming preconditions the BactoSense with the sample. Priming can be used to reduce the carryover of cells or unwanted substances, and takes approximately 5 minutes.

blocks.html: Use a Prime under the following circumstances:

blocks.text: After a Clean Sampling Device protocol (with and without Washstation) After measuring a sample with a high chlorine concentration or any other unwanted substance which may affect subsequent measurements

blocks.text: WORK STEP 1. Make sure the manual sampling device is tightly installed as described in Installation of the manual sampling device . 2. Navigate to the Home screen of the BactoSense user interface. 3. On the Home screen, press Mode and select Manual mode. Press Back, then Measure to open the measurement wizard. 4. Select Prime from the list of available protocols. 5. Press the Next button. 6. Attach the sample you want to measure next to the manual sampling device. 7. Press the Start button.
